* test(e2e): add lifecycle markers, a preload scenario and replace-source controls

Ports the player lifecycle cases from #4743 into the test app, as markers:

- evt-initial-idle: player.status read in the setup callback, before any load.
- evt-status-loading / evt-status-ready / evt-ready-after-loading: the status
  machine and its order. A player that reports readyToPlay without loading
  first sets the two plain markers but never the third.
- evt-duration-fixture: onLoad reports the 8 s fixture length (+-1 s).
- evt-onLoad-repeated / evt-reloaded-from-start / evt-onEnded-repeated: a
  replacement source loads, starts from 0 and plays through. The restart is
  judged on the first onProgress after the second onLoad, like the seek
  markers judge the first progress after onSeek.
- evt-replace-resolved / evt-replace-rejected and evt-idle-after-release:
  replaceSourceAsync() outcomes. Android also reports idle at the natural
  end of a clip, so idle counts as released only after replaceSourceAsync(null)
  was requested.

New scenario mp4-preload starts with preload() instead of initialize()+play().
New controls btn-replace-hls (awaits replaceSourceAsync(hls), then play() from
JS, so a flow needs a single tap on an idle player) and btn-replace-null.

* test(e2e): cover status order, preload, replaceSourceAsync and release

Four cases from #4743, as Maestro flows on the existing markers:

- smoke-mp4-happy-path additionally asserts idle -> loading -> readyToPlay
  and the fixture duration.
- smoke-preload: readyToPlay without playback, then one play tap plays the
  clip through.
- smoke-replace-source: after the mp4 ends, replaceSourceAsync(hls) resolves,
  a second onLoad arrives, playback restarts from 0 and reaches a second end.
- smoke-release-source: replaceSourceAsync(null) resolves, the player reports
  idle, no error. Whether it can load again is left out on purpose: the docs
  and both native players disagree (see e2e/CONTEXT.md).

* docs(e2e): note the Android idle-at-end quirk and the reuse-after-release question

* test(e2e): anchor the lifecycle markers to their requests, read the status after release

Review follow-ups on the first version of these flows:

- A released player reports nothing: both native players detach every
  emitter listener while releasing, before they set the idle status, and
  Android already reports idle at the natural end of a clip. The release
  scenario now calls replaceSourceAsync(null) from JS during playback (so it
  also proves the release stops playback, and needs no tap) and then reads
  player.status, which is what the #4743 test did; evt-idle-after-release is
  derived from that read. The btn-replace-null control is gone with it.
- Android re-emits onLoad on every re-buffer and replay, so "a second
  onLoad" proved nothing. The replacement markers (evt-replacement-loaded,
  evt-reloaded-from-start, evt-ended-after-replace) only count events after
  replaceSourceAsync(source) was requested.
- evt-ready-after-loading judges only the first readyToPlay, so a later
  re-buffer cannot satisfy it retroactively. The two plain status markers it
  was derived from were not asserted by any flow and are private state now.
- The play() after a replacement runs outside the promise chain's rejection
  handler, so its failure can no longer be logged as the replacement
  rejecting.
- The restart threshold has its own constant (RELOAD_START_SECONDS).

* test(e2e): wait for readyToPlay after onLoad in the mp4 happy path

iOS reports onLoad as soon as the AVPlayerItem is ready and readyToPlay only
once the buffer allows playback (or when playback starts), a moment later. The
flow asserted evt-ready-after-loading right after evt-onLoad and failed on the
iOS leg of the first run; it now waits for it, as smoke-preload already did.

* docs(e2e): replaceSourceAsync(null) releasing the player is documented, not open

* test(e2e): quarantine the status-order check (iOS readyToPlay, #5155)

On iOS the readyToPlay status is sometimes never reported although the clip
plays to its end: the same flow passed on one CI run and failed on the next
with no code change (status stays loading from the item assignment to
onEnded). The idle -> loading -> readyToPlay assertion moves from the mp4
happy path into smoke-status-order.yaml, tagged flaky, which runs in the
nightly quarantine leg and not in the gate (CONTEXT.md, zero-retries rule).
The happy path keeps evt-initial-idle and evt-duration-fixture, which are
reported with onLoad itself.

* test(e2e): make the quarantine tripwire list the quarantined flows with their issues

The matrix-plan test asserted that no committed flow is quarantined, as a
tripwire for the first quarantine. smoke-status-order.yaml is the first:
the test now keeps the list of quarantined flows and requires each to cite
its issue, so a tag cannot be added or kept without one. CI_MATRIX_DESIGN.md
